{{main article|2023 WTA Tour}}

The WTA 1000 Mandatory and non-Mandatory tournaments, which are part of the [[WTA 1000 tournaments]], make up the elite tour for professional women's [[tennis]] organised by the [[Women's Tennis Association|WTA]] called the [[WTA Tour]]. There are four 1000 Mandatory tournaments: Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid and Beijing and five non-Mandatory tournaments: Dubai, Rome, Canada, Cincinnati and Guadalajara, the last of which continuing from the previous year as the replacement for the Wuhan Open.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 Tournaments {{!}} WTA Official |url=https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/2023 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201225544/https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/2023 |archive-date=1 December 2022|website=Women's Tennis Association |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rohit |date=16 November 2022 |title=Tennis Schedule 2023: Complete ATP and WTA tennis tour calendar for 2022-23 |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/tennis-schedule-2023-complete-atp-wta-tennis-tour-calendar-2022-23 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201232208/https://www.sportskeeda.com/tennis/tennis-schedule-2023-complete-atp-wta-tennis-tour-calendar-2022-23 |archive-date=2022-12-01 |access-date= |website=www.sportskeeda.com |language=en-us}}</ref>
